blocks.heading: I am not in the business of making people louder.
blocks.subheading: I help leaders who have already done the work make that work legible to the people who decide things.

blocks.eyebrow: The moment this became a method
blocks.moment: He read the acquisition announcement out loud in the boardroom, put the page down, and said: they didn't even know we existed.
blocks.aftermath: Our product was better. Our margins were better. Our founder had been building in that category for eleven years. The company that won had a chief executive with a book, a podcast, and a phrase that everyone in the industry had started repeating. I had spent four years writing accurate sentences about a man nobody could recall.

blocks.heading: How I got here
blocks.markdown:
I started in corporate communications in 2009, which was a strange time to start. The trade I had trained for — press releases, embargoes, careful relationships with twelve journalists — was quietly being replaced by something nobody had a name for yet. My job was to protect executives from attention. Within five years my job was to manufacture it.

I was good at the mechanics and increasingly uneasy about the results. We could reliably generate coverage. We could not reliably generate **standing**. Those are different things, and confusing them is the central error of the personal branding industry.

### What I noticed

Between 2014 and 2018 I worked with roughly forty senior executives across logistics, healthcare and financial services. The ones whose reputations compounded had almost nothing in common stylistically. Some were charismatic; several were not. Some published constantly; two published roughly four times a year.

What they shared was structural:

1. They had a **position** narrow enough to be repeated by someone else accurately.
2. They had **evidence** they could produce on demand, with numbers attached.
3. They had a **named method** that travelled without them in the room.
4. They were **present in a small number of the right places**, not in all places.

Everything I do now is an attempt to reproduce those four conditions deliberately rather than accidentally. That is the whole method. It is not complicated. It is just unusual to do in the correct order.

### What I believe about this work

Authority built on evidence is durable. Authority built on exposure is a treadmill, and the treadmill speeds up. I would rather help six people a year build the first kind than sixty build the second.

I live in San Francisco. I have advised leaders in nineteen countries. I write about this most weeks, badly at first and then better after editing, which is also roughly how I advise clients to work.
